questions.prompt: For the input ["u-3", "u-1", "u-3", "u-2", "u-1"], what is the output, and what in your implementation ensures that repeated IDs do not change the order?
questions.evidence: Independently predicted u-3, u-1, u-2 and explained that duplicate IDs are not added again, preserving the original insertion order.

questions.prompt: For n input entries and k distinct IDs, what are the expected time cost and the memory costs of your Set and returned array? Explain what changes when every input ID is the same.
questions.evidence: Correctly combined O(n) input processing and O(k) distinct-value work as O(n), and retained O(n) time for identical IDs; gave the valid worst-case O(n) memory bound without separating Set/output O(k) storage or the constant-space all-identical case.
